snippet.title: 2026 Total Solar Eclipse (Official NASA Trailer)
snippet.description:
The Sun and Moon are coming together to put on a show for Earth, and we'll be sharing it with you.

On Aug. 12, 2026, a total solar eclipse will be visible in parts of Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, the Atlantic Ocean, Spain, and a small corner of Portugal.

Viewers in other places in the Northern Hemisphere will also have the chance to experience a partial solar eclipse, including parts of the U.S. (from Alaska to North Carolina), most of Canada, much of Europe, and northwestern Africa.

We'll be broadcasting the eclipse live, so you can experience totality from anywhere.

Learn how to watch totality live with us: https://go.nasa.gov/4ftKdXd
Learn more about this solar spectacle: https://science.nasa.gov/eclipses/future-eclipses/total-solar-eclipse-on-august-12-2026/

Credit: NASA

snippet.title: Nyancho - DUWOLO - (Official Music Video)
snippet.description:
DUWOLU – Official Music Video by Nyancho

“Duwolu”, a Mandinka word meaning (Vultures) is the latest powerful social commentary from Gambian artist Nyancho.
Following the message of Wulolu, Duwolu continues Nyancho’s call for unity, peace, justice, accountability, and a better future for The Gambia. The song gives a voice to the frustrations and struggles experienced by ordinary Gambians, particularly young people and those whose voices are often unheard.
The message of Duwolu is not intended as an accusation against the Government or any individual. Rather, it is an appeal and a reminder that many ordinary citizens are struggling and deserve better opportunities, security, justice, and dignity.
Over the years, Gambians have witnessed public discussions and allegations surrounding corruption, misuse of public resources, unexplained wealth, and the disappearance or mismanagement of public funds. We have also seen questions raised about how some individuals who lived modestly for many years later acquired significant wealth, expensive vehicles, and large properties after entering positions of influence.

There have also been concerns about public officials who have spoken against corruption or challenged wrongdoing and subsequently lost their positions. Whether through political disagreements, institutional decisions, or other circumstances, these situations have raised important questions about accountability and transparency.

At the same time, our communities continue to face serious challenges. Innocent people have lost their lives to crime, while many families continue to seek answers and justice. Tribal and divisive rhetoric has also become a concern, with words that can create tension and threaten the unity that Gambians have worked hard to preserve.

And perhaps most importantly, our young people are struggling.
Youth unemployment remains a major challenge. Many young Gambians see irregular migration as their only path toward a better life, risking their lives on dangerous journeys instead of finding opportunities at home. Every young person who leaves represents not only a personal loss, but potentially the loss of a future leader, entrepreneur, artist, professional, or community builder.
